2026-12-27.title: The Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph · Feast
readings: Your heir shall be your own son
The Lord remembers his covenant for ever
The faith of Abraham, Sarah and Isaac
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom
2026-12-27.alt: Year B. These readings may be replaced by those common to all years: Sirach 3:2–6, 12–14; Psalm 128; Colossians 3:12–21. Liturgical colour: white. Sunday within the Octave of Christmas.
2026-12-27.verse: The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favor of God was upon him.
theo: On the Sunday after Christmas the Church looks at the home in which the Son of God chose to grow up. He did not come as an adult from nowhere; he came as a child into a family, with a mother, a foster father, a village, relatives and the Law of Moses. The Second Vatican Council calls the family “the domestic church” (Lumen Gentium 11), and the Holy Family of Nazareth is its model.

This year's readings put faith at the centre of family life. Abraham, childless and old, is told to look at the stars: “So shall your descendants be.” And “he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.” Sarah conceives Isaac at the time God had promised. Hebrews praises their faith: Abraham set out “not knowing where he was going”, and later offered Isaac, trusting that God could raise the dead. A family is built not first on money or plans but on trust in God's promise.

In the Gospel, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple to present him to the Lord, as the Law prescribed for the firstborn (Exodus 13:2), offering the gift of the poor, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”. Simeon takes the child in his arms and blesses God; he also tells Mary that her son will be “a sign that will be opposed” and that “a sword will pierce your own soul too”. Even the Holy Family was not spared sorrow. Then they return to Nazareth, where “the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom”. The hidden years at Nazareth sanctify ordinary family life: work, prayer, obedience and love (CCC 531–533).
conn: The phrase goes back to St John Chrysostom and was taken up by Vatican II (Lumen Gentium 11; CCC 1655–1658). Parents are the first teachers of the faith.
Leviticus 12:8 allowed a poor family to offer two birds instead of a lamb. Mary and Joseph offered the gift of the poor, while presenting the true Lamb of God.

The Law required the redemption of the firstborn son (Exodus 13:2, 12–13) and the purification of the mother forty days after birth (Leviticus 12). The Church celebrates this scene again on 2 February.
Hebrews 11:19 says that Abraham received Isaac back “figuratively speaking” from the dead. The Fathers saw in Isaac carrying the wood a figure of Christ carrying his Cross.
Simeon and Anna stand for faithful Israel waiting for God's promise. The young family and the old saints meet in the Temple.
Jesus spent about thirty years in Nazareth and only about three in public ministry. Most of the life of the Saviour was ordinary family life.
altar: The family gathers around the altar each Sunday as the family of God. Children learn the faith first by seeing their parents pray and receive the Eucharist.
At the Presentation, Jesus is offered to the Father in the Temple. At every Mass he offers himself to the Father, and we offer our families with him.

fathers: He urged Christian parents to make their home a church, where the Scriptures are read and prayers are said together.
He called Nazareth a school of silence, of family life and of work, where we learn what the life of Jesus was like.
magis: The family as the domestic church.
St John Paul II, Familiaris Consortio 86
“The future of humanity passes by way of the family.”
The Holy Family of Nazareth as model for families.
The hidden life at Nazareth; the domestic church.

2026-12-27.prayer: O God, who were pleased to give us the shining example of the Holy Family, graciously grant that we may imitate them in practising the virtues of family life and in the bonds of charity, and so, in the joy of your house, delight one day in eternal rewards. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you grew in wisdom and grace in the home of Mary and Joseph. On this feast of the Holy Family, bless our families. Amen.

Simeon and Anna waited faithfully for years (Luke 2:25, 36–37). What can the elderly teach my family?
What would make our home more like Nazareth?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, two days ago we knelt before the manger. Today the Church asks us to look around the manger: at Mary, at Joseph, at the family into which God chose to be born.

God could have come in any way he wished. He chose to come as a baby, into a family. He needed a mother to feed him, a father to protect him and teach him a trade, and a home where he could grow. That tells us how much God values the family.

Today's first reading shows Abraham and Sarah, old and childless. God tells Abraham to count the stars: so many will be your descendants. And Abraham believed. A family is not built first on property, jobs or plans, but on faith in God.

In the Gospel, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple. They are poor; they can only offer two small birds. Simeon takes the child in his arms and praises God, but also tells Mary that a sword will pierce her heart. Even the Holy Family knew sorrow, fear and uncertainty. If your family is going through hard times, you are not far from Nazareth.

Then the Gospel says simply: they went home to Nazareth, and the child grew, filled with wisdom, and the favour of God was upon him. Thirty quiet years of work, prayer and ordinary love. That is where holiness grows for most of us: at the kitchen table, at work, in patience with each other.
So let us bring our families to the Lord today. Let us pray together at home, forgive each other quickly, respect our elders and bless our children. Jesus, Mary and Joseph, make our homes like yours.
kids: Children, Jesus had a family too: Mary his mother and Joseph his foster father.
He helped Joseph in the carpenter's shop and helped Mary at home.
He obeyed them and grew big and strong and wise.
How can you help at home this week? Maybe tidy your room, or help set the table, with a smile!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this feast of the Holy Family let us look at the one member who never says a word in the Gospels: St Joseph. Mary speaks, Jesus speaks, angels speak, but Joseph only listens and acts.

Four times an angel speaks to Joseph in a dream, and four times he obeys at once: to take Mary as his wife, to flee to Egypt, to return to the land of Israel, and to settle in Nazareth (Matthew 1:20; 2:13, 19, 22). Each time the Gospel says simply that Joseph got up and did as he was told. In a world full of noise, Joseph teaches us to listen to God in silence and to act without delay.

Joseph was a protector. When Herod sought to kill the child, Joseph took the child and his mother by night and fled to Egypt (Matthew 2:14). Think of that journey: a refugee family, poor, in a foreign land, with a little baby. Joseph worked with his hands to feed them. Today many fathers work far from home, in the Gulf or abroad, to support their families. Joseph understands them.

The Gospel calls Joseph a just man (Matthew 1:19). When he discovered that Mary was with child, he did not want to expose her to public disgrace. His justice was full of mercy. In our families too, justice and tenderness must go together: correction without humiliation, firmness without harshness, forgiveness without weakness.

Fathers, look at Joseph: protect your families, work honestly, pray, bless your children. Mothers, look at Mary. Children, look at Jesus, who was obedient to His parents. And let every family here entrust itself to St Joseph, guardian of the Redeemer. May he who guarded the Holy Family guard ours too.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Second Vatican Council gave the Christian family a beautiful name: the domestic church (Lumen Gentium 11). On the feast of the Holy Family, let us see what this means in practice.

A church is a place where God is worshipped, His Word is heard and love is lived. The home is meant to be exactly that. Parents are the first heralds of the faith for their children (CCC 1656). Long before catechism class, children learn from their parents how to make the sign of the cross, how to fold their hands, how to forgive. Moses told the Israelites to speak of God's words at home and on the road, when lying down and when rising (Deuteronomy 6:7).

The Fourth Commandment teaches children to honour their father and mother, with respect, gratitude, obedience while they are young, and care for them when they are old (CCC 2214–2220; Sirach 3:1–14). It also gives parents duties: to educate their children in faith, in prayer and in virtue, to respect their vocation, and to give the example of a good life (CCC 2221–2226). St Paul writes: fathers, do not provoke your children, or they may lose heart (Colossians 3:21).

Families today are under great pressure: work far from home, financial stress, screens that keep everyone apart in the same room, addiction, broken marriages. The Holy Family also knew danger, poverty and exile. They survived because God was at the centre. Let our families do the same: pray together every evening, even briefly; eat at least one meal a day together without phones; come to the Holy Mass together on Sunday; forgive before sleeping.

And let the parish be a family of families, supporting those who are struggling, single parents, widows, the elderly living alone. May Jesus, Mary and Joseph bless every family in this parish, and make our homes true domestic churches.

intro: Theme: “The child grew and became strong.”
A family of faith, a child presented to the Lord, and the hidden holiness of Nazareth.

sub: Abraham and Sarah were old and childless.
God promised descendants like the stars.
Faith is the foundation of the home.
q: He brought him outside and said, “Look toward heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your descendants be.” And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Begin or renew daily family prayer.

sub: The firstborn belongs to God.
Mary and Joseph offer the gift of the poor.
Simeon foretells the sword.
q: Consecrate to me all the firstborn; whatever is the first to open the womb among the Israelites, of human beings and animals, is mine.

Then Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.”
points.apply: Offer your children to God in prayer today.

sub: Jesus obeyed Mary and Joseph.
He grew in wisdom and grace.
Faith is passed on at home.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.

Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart. And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
points.apply: Read a Gospel passage together at home this week.

concl: God chose a family; families find God at home.
Jesus, Mary and Joseph, make our homes like yours.
